General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cosmopolitan ↗ Open Full Page

These Thanksgiving Hairstyles Are Perfect for Everything From Friendsgiving to Family Dinner

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (921 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, thanksgiving is one of those holidays where I wanna look cute, but I also have approximately one million other things to worry about.
  • Luckily, I found a bunch of Thanksgiving-worthy hairstyles prove that looking put together doesn’t have to equal time-consuming.
  • There’s nothing quite as classic as a big, bouncy blowout.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, thanksgiving is one of those holidays where I wanna look cute, but I also have approximately one million other things to worry about. Between figuring out what to wear, preparing dinner, and making sure the table is set, I’m also trying to look fashionable and stay comfortable. Ideally, I want to do both of those things without spending hours styling my outfit or my hair.

Luckily, I found a bunch of Thanksgiving-worthy hairstyles prove that looking put together doesn’t have to equal time-consuming. Plus, since you’re amongst family and friends, the holiday is the perfect excuse to experiment with some latest or elevated styles. Think bouncy blowouts and sleek buns that pair perfectly with your favorite fall sweater or half-up styles finished with velvet bows for a lil holiday flair. Ahead, the cutest Thanksgiving hairstyles to screenshot now. I promise these are quick, effortless, and totally chic, so they won’t take you away from your food, football, or family for too long.

There’s nothing quite as classic as a big, bouncy blowout. Use a round brush and hair dryer or a blow dryer blush of your choice to get these voluminous waves à la Sabrina Carpenter. This big, glossy volume looks especially great with a fall sweater.

It has been revealed that A festive accessory makes a simple style feel so special. Channel your inner J.Lo with this sleek half-up, half-down look, finished off with a velvet bow to get in the holiday spirit.

Take a cue from Olivia Dean and let your natural curls do the talking this Thanksgiving. These voluminous ringlets are equal parts effortless and glamorous. Work some mousse into your roots, scrunch to define your curls, and diffuse your hair for maximum bounce and body.

Sources indicate that ponytails are great, but give the classic look a playful upgrade with a bubble braid that’s cute and easy to recreate. Simply secure your hair into a ponytail, add elastics every few inches, and gently tug each section out to create the bubble effect. It’s a fun, trendy option for Thanksgiving that keeps your hair out of your face.

Recent findings suggest that leave it to Anya Taylor-Joy to make a simple braid look totally elegant. This low side braid proves that you don’t need an elaborate updo to make a statement. Braid your hair loosely on one side and secure with an elastic—you can opt for a discreet clear one for a subtle finish, add an elastic in a autumnal shade for a more festive finish, or really go all out by clipping a bow on the end. Either way, it’s a perfect Thanksgiving hairstyle that takes just moments to create.

Hailey Bieber can make even the seemingly simplest hairstyle look super chic, and her flippy bob is no exception. Channel her style with a retro-inspired sleek bob with ends that flip outward for some extra movement. Recreate the look with a round brush and blow-dryer or a flat iron, curling the ends away from your face.

It has been revealed that why settle for one braid when you can have two? Double braided ponytails are a playful way to switch up your Thanksgiving hairstyle. The how-to is simple: Split your ponytail into two pieces and braid each length separately.

It has been revealed that effortlessly cool, a half-up, half-down hairstyle is proof that sometimes less really is more. It’s the perfect balance between polished and undone, keeping hair away from the face while letting the rest of the lengths flow freely. It’s an especially chic and easy option for Thanksgiving dinner that’s Zoe Kravitz-approved.

Nobody does quiet luxury beauty quite like Sofia Richie Grainge, and her signature slicked-back low bun is the definition of understated elegance. You can get the look for yourself for your Thanksgiving hairstyle: Create a clean center part, smooth your hair back with styling gel or cream, and twist it into a low bun at the nape of your neck. It’s sophisticated, timeless, and practically guaranteed to survive the whole night, from appetizers to dinner to dessert.

Industry observers note that sometimes the chicest hairstyles are also the easiest. Case in point: a French twist with a claw clip. For a Thanksgiving-ready take on the classic French twist, gather your hair at the nape of your neck, twist it upward, and secure it with your favorite claw clip. Leave a few face-framing pieces loose for an effortlessly undone finish, or slick everything back for a more polished look.

Ayo Edebiri makes intricate braids look effortlessly cool. Her sew-in-inspired braided design adds a little extra personality to a classic protective style. It’s a chic option for Thanksgiving festivities, especially if you want a hairstyle that makes a statement without requiring much day-of styling. Plus, the intricate detailing means your hair practically doubles as an accessory.

In a recent development, this relaxed half-up, half-down hairstyle is proof that you don't need a complicated updo to look put together for Thanksgiving. The effortless style lets you pull back the top section of your hair with an oversized leopard print bow (animal print is so in this season). It’s the perfect balance between casual and chic.

It has been revealed that catharine Malzahn is a contributing beauty writer at Cosmo. She’s written about all things hair, from cool hair color trends to the best haircuts worth trying.

From the Archive: Ina Garten Tapped a Few Famous Friends for Her '90s Farmhouse Renovation

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Welcome to Archive Dive—my upcoming excuse to obsess over the absolute treasures hiding in House Beautiful’s 130-year-old archives.
  • In a recent development, after Ina Garten moved the now-shuttered Barefoot Contessa specialty store from Westhampton to East Hampton, she and her husband, Jeffrey, decided to put down roots in the neighborhood.
  • In our latest Archive Dive, we revisit the 1994 renovation, which includes Garten’s search for the right paint color, her no-nonsense decorating approach, and her love of the property’s grounds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Welcome to Archive Dive—my upcoming excuse to obsess over the absolute treasures hiding in House Beautiful’s 130-year-old archives. Every month, we’ll dig up a favorite story from the past (epic room makeovers, wildly bold design swings, and style moments that were way ahead of their time) and talk about why they still resonate today. It’s part history lesson, part design deep-dive, and 100 percent a love letter to the iconic taste that’s defined HB for over a century.—Jo Saltz, House Beautiful Editor in Chief.

In a recent development, after Ina Garten moved the now-shuttered Barefoot Contessa specialty store from Westhampton to East Hampton, she and her husband, Jeffrey, decided to put down roots in the neighborhood. But rather than buy a fresh-build home, Garten transformed an old farmhouse into a light-filled, five-room retreat designed for hosting—and feeding—guests.

In our latest Archive Dive, we revisit the 1994 renovation, which includes Garten’s search for the right paint color, her no-nonsense decorating approach, and her love of the property’s grounds. She took each project in stride with help from famous friends like Martha Stewart and the late interior designer Robert Currie—and Jeffrey, of course. The result was a relaxed home with an entertaining-ready atmosphere and a garden that would make any green-thumbed foodie proud. Read on for the original story.

With the help of Robert Currie, the owner of a fabulous food emporium in the Hamptons planned her nearby house for the casual ease of the legions of guests she feeds in her spare time.

Are you full of self-doubt in the dark of the night? Should you buy that old house? Should you change your career? Then follow in Ina Garten’s (bare) footsteps. She has done both with such breathtaking speed and success that the average worrier blinks in awe. She bought a Westhampton, Upcoming York, specialty store (oddly shaped breads, ravishing vegetables, seafood salad to go) from a business opportunities ad practically on the spot.

“I didn’t know how to slice smoked salmon or tell whether the Brie was ripe,” she confesses. But in no time, she turned her emporium, Barefoot Contessa, into a foodie’s fairyland.

Recent findings suggest that after Garten moved the store to East Hampton she converted a cramped, run-down old farmhouse in the village into an airy five-room refuge and party venue for herself and her husband. “I just trusted that if the house had good ‘bones,’ I could figure it all out,” she laughs. No insomnia. No agonies. And, incredibly, no mistakes.

Recent findings suggest that she’s a nurturer, too, a definite Earth Mother, which is certainly why she fled her career in nuclear energy policy planning for the far more congenial field of food. Her personal policy is summed up simply: lots of entertaining.

Recent findings suggest that when her husband—a former Columbia professor, author, and investment banker—worked in Upcoming York, she encouraged his uptight fellow bankers to loosen their ties and shed their jackets by dishing up platters of fried chicken and other finger foods. In East Hampton she gives Sunday afternoon parties with plenty of easy food “like crabcake sandwiches,” and leaves all the doors open so guests will feel free to wander out and eat on the porch, or anywhere else that seems inviting.

It has been revealed that she often serves in her sunny kitchen, which contains the requisite serious fridge and stove, but lacks the usual array of self-important utensils. This is a kitchen with nothing to prove.

The toughest decisions of her fix-up were the wall colors. She thought at first that she might like the whole house vanilla (a true foodie’s choice), but test patches were too white or yellow.

Recent findings suggest that “I had samples all over the walls, and the painter was yelling ‘Stop already’,” but finally she hit on a toasty khaki for her bedroom. She was still stuck for the first floor when she spotted the bedroom primer paint: khaki halved with white. A mental lightbulb turned on, and the painter went to work. The house is now two values of that changeable shade with browny greens in the upholstery derived from the tapestry-covered living room sofa.

Industry observers note that there is not a stick of unnecessary furniture in the farmhouse either, just several old oversize tables, a few pieces of portly upholstery, and in the bedroom, a brass bed (of which a friend noted, “That’s not a bed, it’s a temple”), plus two chairs. No windows are curtained.

It has been revealed that “Everything,” Garten feels, “should do something, have a function, not just sit there. I like things to be spare.” And bare as well, like her new floors, which are crafted of newly purchased old wood. Are the original floors still underneath? Nope. With a sanding and a coat of polyurethane, they are reincarnated as a kitchen countertop.

Garten actually bought the house for its grounds, because she yearned to garden. She had lived for a time in rented houses, but when she found herself planting expensive trees in rented lawns, she realized it was time to own some land.

Outside her kitchen doors she has cut square beds for tomatoes, which mix quite cheerfully with dahlias, and for roses knee-deep in catmint. She likes to combine “mess with structure,” but her structures are always imaginative. Instead of a single stake for each tomato plant, for instance, she does a row of tepees. Or she lines her disheveled strawberry beds with a spine of iris.

Recent findings suggest that A Manhattan florist friend, Tom Pritchard of Pure Mädderlake, helped her with the garden design and did a very clever thing. He took two chairs out into the garden and walked around with her, scoping out the best seating spots. That’s how she decided which vistas to emphasize and which had too fine a view of the neighbor’s patio. Gardening has become a passion since she moved here. Every surface in her house is piled with well-thumbed horticultural tomes; for the time being, her food banks are relegated to the bottom of the pile.

Garten acknowledges that she has had a lot of help. Her good friend, the late Robert Currie, designed all the seating, shopped with her, and arranged the furniture. He also taught her to avoid like mad “anything that was too trendy.” Stephen Scanniello, the rose dean at the Brooklyn Botanic Garden, chose a hundred great roses for her, and Martha Stewart passed judgment on her upcoming shower stall. No less helpful was her very supportive husband.

In a recent development, but husbands don’t ponder that midnight ceiling with you. And talented friends aren’t around at 2 a.m., when the real bullets are bitten. Some lucky people, though, do it all with ease—Ina Garten for one. Warm and comfy, like her own upcoming house, she just turns over and goes back to sleep.

Tech Report: Ezra Frech and Connor Wood Are the Final Boys

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2377 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that one of the best things to come out of Dancing With the Stars season 35?
  • It has been revealed that despite premiering over 21 years ago, the show is presently experiencing a major modern resurgence, and social media engagement is to thank.
  • And it’s also thanks to social media that fans have gotten a front-row seat to Connor and Ezra’s off-camera bond.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that one of the best things to come out of Dancing With the Stars season 35? After Guillermo Rodriguez’s assisted knee walks and the chaotic Cat in the Hat dance routine following Tyler Cameron’s baby gender reveal, it’s got to be Ezra Frech and Connor Wood’s unexpected bromance.

It has been revealed that despite premiering over 21 years ago, the show is presently experiencing a major modern resurgence, and social media engagement is to thank. The show has tapped into younger audiences both with its casting choices and through daily behind-the-scenes clips, to the point where even A-listers like Jennifer Lawrence can recognize Connor drinking a smoothie on the street. (By the way, if you’re wondering whether J. Law has reached out to him since he paid her no mind, the answer is sadly no. “I beat that horse to death,” Connor notes. “I’m sure she’s like, ‘Can this guy let it go?’”).

And it’s also thanks to social media that fans have gotten a front-row seat to Connor and Ezra’s off-camera bond. What began with a TikTok poking fun at the fact that Connor’s nickname is Fibula and Ezra was born without his left fibula (which was all Ezra’s idea, according to Connor) has blossomed into an iconic friendship. Now, the besties must face off as the two remaining male stars heading into the finale—but they’re not going to let a little competition come between them.

Sources indicate that “Ezra is definitely more competitive,” Connor, who’s paired with Rylee Arnold, tells Cosmopolitan. “He’s got a fighting spirit. When we get to eliminations, I’m thinking about my post-show quesadilla. I mean, obviously I want to stay in the competition. But I’ve considered every week that I’ve made it a win. The only person I’m competitive with is myself because I want to get this right.”.

According to recent reports, “This is a competition show, but you’re kind of rooting for everybody else and want everyone else to do well,” Ezra, who’s partnered with Daniella Karagach, adds. “Plus, there’s so much that’s out of your control. I want Connor to succeed. He wants me to succeed. You know, it’s real love.”.

The first time the two met was at the promo photo shoot ahead of the season premiere, where the connection was so instantaneous that Connor thought they must already know each other. As Connor explains, “We’re hugging, we’re chatting, and then I’m walking away like, ‘Oh my gosh, where did I meet him before?’ Turns out, it was our first time meeting. We just connected straight off the bat.”.

“Sometimes you’ll meet somebody and just click and know like, ‘Oh, that’s somebody I’m gonna be friends with,’” claims Ezra of that fateful first meeting. “I’m sure Connor and I would have definitely hit it off and become really close in any other context—but I think Dancing With the Stars accelerated that timeline because we’re both way out of our comfort zone. For us to be in this together, it’s bonded us in a very unique way.”.

They may be a decade apart in age (Connor is 31 as of September, while Ezra was born a month before DWTS first premiered in 2005) and come from two entirely different worlds (Connor is a podcaster and comedian, while Ezra is a two-time Paralympian with two gold medals to prove it), but their friendship? From post-rehearsal dance parties to spray tan dates to trailer talks, it knows no bounds.

Cosmopolitan caught up with Ezra and Connor ahead of the DWTS season 35 finale to chat about beating the odds, blocking out the noise, and what happens after they leave the ballroom.

Industry observers note that connor: I thought there was more to the sentence. I thought I would hear, “Connor and Rylee, come down here and dance for us again.” I literally walked backstage after they called mine and Rylee’s name, and I took off my jacket and just sat on the ground. I was in shock.

Ezra: They do say names are called in no particular order, but when I was standing there with Harry [Shum Jr.], I was just like, “Wow, this is crazy.” No one will tell you that they’re standing up there feeling confident, so when they leave you up there longer, it definitely makes you sweat.

Connor: I’m an extrovert, but it’s very selective. I don’t do emotions. Being on the show, I’ve put out a more vulnerable me. I’ve been sharing things on national TV that I don’t even share with my friends, and it’s been wildly uncomfortable in the best way. You know, I’ve always found work for myself that’s come really easy to me—like, comedy has been natural for me. This is nothing like that. This is the hardest I’ve ever worked in my life, and my brain chemistry has been changed forever because of this.

Ezra: I didn’t come in with any dance experience, and quite frankly, I thought I had natural limitations on what I was capable of on the dance floor. What Dani has brought out of me is almost rewiring the limitations I placed on myself and changing my own expectations of what I can do on a prosthetic—which is crazy, because I’ve lived 21 years and felt like I had a pretty good understanding of what I was capable of on my own prosthetic leg. Then I come on Dancing With the Stars and meet Dani and that completely shifts.

It has been revealed that connor: [laughs] You think I’m watching myself? Oh, no. I don’t watch. And the choreo has been hard, but it’s gotten easier each week for me to learn dances. Like, learning the week 3 samba, I’m like, “Rylee, pack your bags. It’s been great getting to know you.” But now I know that I’ll get it.

Ezra: Yeah, I don’t really watch. I mean, I end up seeing clips, and earlier in the season, I would rewatch the dances. But everything’s happening so fast; it’s hard to, like, really sit and marinate on them when you gotta refocus for the next week. The cool thing is these dances will live forever. They’re out there in the world, and I will be able to watch and appreciate those moments and have pride in them for the rest of my life.

Connor: Michael Scott said it best: “Do I need to be liked? Absolutely not. I like to be liked. I enjoy being liked. I have to be liked.” I relate to that so much, because I’ll want to reach out to someone and be like, “Do you really hate me? Like, walk me through what I did during my jive that has made you just despise me?” I don’t think these people actually have that much hatred in their heart. I think they’re really invested fans, and it’s part of the game. Would I slide into someone’s DMs and say, “Watch your back”? No. But I know it’s what I signed up for.

It has been revealed that ezra: People online—as far as whether they think you’re great or mediocre or suck or whatever the opinions are on social media—shouldn’t influence your day-to-day. Thankfully, for Dani and I, there haven’t been too many negative comments, but, of course, with every 30 positive comments, you’re going to get a negative comment. It’s all about not letting that little negative comment overshadow the beautiful stuff that people are saying online as well.

Sources indicate that connor: This is a once-in-a-lifetime chance, but it’s also objectively fun. It’s a show about dancing. I’m not going to make a joke of it, but there’s humor involved. It’s so important to take a step back and laugh sometimes. This is fun. It should be fun.

Industry observers note that connor: You do it anxious. You know, there are people like Ezra with serious uphill battles, and he’s crushing it. I’m just here with anxiety and ADHD and small amounts of OCD and dancing on TV. It’s just something that I’ve always dealt with. I go into standup anxious, and honestly, I think it helps me operate. It pushes me to make sure I get in all of my rehearsal hours so that there’s nothing to be anxious about. As my dad told me, “If you weren’t anxious, you would be anxious.”.

Industry observers note that ezra: I think the way we phrase things in our head controls the way we feel about them. Yes, it can be a burden to feel like you’re representing a community, but it’s a beautiful burden, and so I don’t see it as a negative thing. I get to play a small role in representing my community on such a special show like Dancing With the Stars—I think it’s actually, like, the pride and joy and honor of my life.

It has been revealed that ezra: No, it’s not in my DNA to chill. I mean, after 2028, I’ll probably take some downtime for sure—but then, you know, you’ve got the next Games in 2032, you’ve got world championships the next year, so there’s never really an end. I’ll probably compete on the track for another 15 years or so. And hopefully after the show ends, I’ll take a nice vacation or just rot for a little bit.

Recent findings suggest that connor: Rylee and Ezra are the same age, and you know, I do feel my age a lot of the time when I talk to them. Like, Rylee only knew who Nicole Kidman was because of the AMC pre-roll ads, and Ezra hadn’t seen High School Musical when we were doing the Wildcats dance. But both of them are so wise beyond their years. As soon as Ezra and I became friends, I started seeing old clips of him at, like, 9 years old on Ellen, and he was probably more eloquent and emotionally mature than I am now. People keep wanting him to be the Bachelor, but I think he needs to run for office. He’s just got this natural charisma.

Ezra: I didn’t listen to his podcast, but I’d seen clips of him online, and I knew of him. There’s a really funny video of a Team USA thing that I did two or three years ago where I’m lip-syncing to Connor’s audio. It’s like, “I have purse; I have shoe.” And now people are like, “Wow, the invisible string theory brought them together.” It’s funny; he’s the exact same online versus in person. He’s the same dude. He’s able to take things in, he’s able to feel them, and then he’s able to articulate them in a way that resonates with people. That’s what makes him so good as a comedian.

Recent findings suggest that connor: There’s this guy in a suit that’s jumping straight up in the air and it looks like an exclamation point. I’d say that’s Ezra, since he’s so elevated in the way he carries himself. And, of course, he’s got hops.

Industry observers note that ezra: I would describe Connor with the emoji that’s smiling and sweating, because he’s always smiling and he’s always kind of sweating, and it’s sort of perfect. Like, he’ll make jokes and then look around like, “Ooh, did that land?”.

It has been revealed that connor: Val [Chmerkovskiy] and Jenna [Johnson] and I are gonna work on hip-hop dance at their studio. Val and I are also doing a standup show together at some point. I just adore Brandon [Armstrong] and Alan [Bersten], too. Us three together? Trouble. Britt [Stewart] and I connected on some zen woo-woo stuff, so we’re gonna hang out. And Jenna Dewan and her partner Steve [Kazee], we’re gonna hang out. Julianne [Hough] and I are gonna hang out in Newly introduced York. I mean, I talk to everybody. I hope I see everybody again.

Sources indicate that ezra: Amber [Glenn] is someone who is a real close part of my life and will be for a long time. I feel like her and I are on the same team together in this with Pasha [Pashkov] and Dani. Guillermo is someone I’m going to be close to forever. Like me, him, and Connor—we’re in the group chat texting all the time. And I love Tyler Cameron, and Harry is the sweetest, and Jenna—like, it’s hard to pick and choose. I could see myself still talking to pretty much everybody on the cast.

Ezra: The internet is crazy. Right now, I’m definitely single but not necessarily looking for a relationship. Because, again, once the dance season ends, I’ll be committing myself entirely to track again. I’m enjoying being single, and it’ll probably stay that way for a while.

Industry observers note that connor: This has been like a study abroad trip. Like, I am fully immersed in a culture that is so far outside of my comfort zone and so far away from what I know. Learning something newly introduced at my age is so rare, let alone at this level on TV with a world-class athlete teaching me. And if it does happen, it probably happens to billionaires’ kids who are, like, paying Serena Williams to do private lessons for two years. I think I’m gonna wake up on Wednesday feeling like I walked out of a loud party and shut the door with my ears still ringing. Like, I’m alone. Party is over. It’s time to go home.

Ezra: I’ll miss getting to see everyone at the rehearsal studio. I’ll miss getting lunch with Dani after practice. I’ll miss getting the opportunity to commit myself to something like this so entirely. And I’m gonna miss the show days. You become so close to everybody, and you spend so much time around these people, and then all of a sudden, it’s going to end. But the good thing is that these people are still going to be in my life. I’m still going to hang out with Dani, and I’m still going to see Connor whenever I can, and we’ll get lunch with Guillermo. These are people I’ll be with forever.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been almost a week since Jenna Johnson and Harry Shum Jr.’s shocking elimination from Dancing With the Stars, and now that she’s had some time to process, Jenna indicates she’s hoping fans of the show can get back to spreading joy instead of online bullying.

“I feel like Dancing with the Stars used to be the show that everyone tuned into to turn off the noise and to just experience two hours of pure joy, and entertainment, and excitement,” she told People. “So it’s sad that this online bullying and hate has become so relevant and intertwined with the show.”.

Jenna certainly isn’t the only person on Dancing With the Stars season 35 to speak out about the increasingly negative vibes on social media.

According to recent reports, harry previously told E! News, “I hope they address that at a certain point. Because I think there’s a good amount of bullying that doesn’t feel really good, and I think the rest of the cast feels it.”.

Meanwhile, Jenna Dewan told Extra when she was eliminated, “I know it’s hard to know how this all plays into it. I know this was a particularly tough week for a lot of the online noise and all stuff that comes with the show. I don’t know, I’ll never know how, or if, any of that plays into this. But I know that we went out there and had the best time of our life.”.

Plenty of shows have had to issue anti-bullying PSAs to their audience ahead of the show (including Love Island and The Summer I Turned Pretty), so it’s possible Dancing With the Stars will follow suit next season.
